 This is the foldable option we prefer at bedside, because the heavy base stays put. The phone and watch modules are angle-adjustable, the bottom has an anti-slip pad, and you can pull the phone off one-handed without the whole stand sliding. Reviewers call that combination out specifically as the reason it works in a bedroom rather than on a tidy desk.
 It charges an iPhone, an Apple Watch, and AirPods at once, with the brand claiming an iPhone 16 and a Series 10 watch reach full in roughly one and a half to two hours. The N52 magnets auto-align both the phone and the watch, which the company says improves charging efficiency by 25 percent.
 The sleep-friendliness is a spec sheet line that turns out to matter: the LED indicator stays weak while charging and does not disturb sleep. Over-voltage, over-current, temperature, and short-circuit protection are all built in. The high-gloss housing does not block the phone camera, so sideways video calls work at the back edge of the base.
 A 20W USB-C charger and a 3.3-foot USB-C cable are in the box, with a one-year warranty. The company notes the 20W adapter is required to hit the advertised charge times, so do not swap it for a phone brick.
 Is the fold actually useful for a bedside setup?
 It is useful if you travel. Flat, it takes up the space of a notepad in a carry-on, and at home it works as a stand for reading in bed with the phone propped up. If you never leave the house, the fold does nothing for you and you are paying for a feature you will not use.
 For overnight use the adjustable angles are the better feature: the phone module tilts for a reading position and the watch module adjusts separately, which is harder to do on a rigid stand.
 What is the compatibility catch?
 The magnetic phone pad only works with MagSafe-equipped iPhones from the 12 through 17 series. There is no magnetic attraction for other phones, so this is not a mixed-ecosystem choice. The watch pad covers Apple Watch Series 11 down to SE and Ultra, and no other smartwatch brand.
 AirPods 2 and 3 need a wireless charging case. Reviewers otherwise like the fold-flat design and the dim indicator, and the included adapter is appreciated in a category where it is so often missing.
 Check Latest Price 
 How to Choose a Wireless Charging Station for Your Nightstand
 Every dock on this list works. The difference between a good nightstand charger and a frustrating one comes down to eight things, and all eight are things you can check before you buy rather than discover on the second night.
 Measure your surface first. A typical bedside table is 12 to 18 inches wide. Compare that to the base of the dock, not the phone stand height, and add an inch of clearance behind for the cable. If the base overhangs, you will knock it with your elbow.
 Count your devices, honestly. A 3-in-1 covers a phone, a watch, and earbuds. A phone, a watch, earbuds, and a second phone for work needs a 7-in-1 or a two-station setup.
 Check the charging standard. Qi2 or MagSafe gives you magnetic alignment and better speed. Plain Qi is the compatibility fallback for older or Android phones.
 Confirm the adapter is included. This is the most repeated complaint in the entire category. Of these eight, seven include a wall charger; the Acer Gadget comes with a cable only.
 Read the case thickness limit. Anything under 5mm is workable. Anything under 2mm means you will be taking your case off every morning, and many people stop using the dock entirely.
 Decide about the light. If you share a room with a light sleeper, you need a dimmable or fully switchable indicator. If a warm glow helps you find your phone, a night light is a feature.
 Look at the watch pad specifically. Only certified fast-charge docks deliver Apple’s claimed watch speeds. Slow watch pads are the most common reason a bedside dock ends up unused.
 Think about the cord. A dock replaces four cables with one. That single cable still has to reach an outlet, so check whether your table has one behind it or a long cord to route.
 If you want to compare standards side by side before you commit, our general guide to wireless charging stations covers the technology in more detail, and if your bedside table is currently doing double duty as a desk, the charging desk lamps we tested solve the same clutter problem in one object.
 Qi vs MagSafe vs Qi2: Which Standard Do You Actually Need?
 Magnetic charging wins on both speed and reliability, and it is the right default in 2026. Plain Qi still earns its place as the compatibility fallback, because it works with more phones. Here is the honest breakdown.
 Qi is the baseline standard, found on flat pads and older stands. It delivers up to 10 to 15W and it is alignment-sensitive, which means the phone has to land in roughly the right spot. Magnetic Qi and Qi2 add magnets that line the coils up automatically, which is why they charge faster and why they do not fail intermittently at 3am.
 MagSafe is Apple’s magnetic alignment system, Qi2-based since the iPhone 12. Qi2 is the newer magnetic standard that reaches higher speeds, and the Anker Prime on this list uses the newest Qi2.2 version at 25W. Any of them needs an iPhone 12 or newer, or a MagSafe case if your phone is older or is an Android handset.
 For overnight charging, 10W is genuinely enough. Faster wattage matters when you want a quick top-up before leaving the house, not when the phone sits on the pad for eight hours. Buy for how you use it rather than for the largest number on the box.
 Are Wireless Chargers Safe to Leave Charging Overnight?
 Yes, provided the unit has foreign object detection and over-temperature protection and carries a recognised certification mark. Most of these picks list over-current, over-voltage and temperature protection, and the GAUOLN and Acer units are FCC certified, while the ANker-branded models carry a 24-month warranty.
 The reports of melted, overheated multi-device stations come almost entirely from cheap unbranded units with no listed protection. That is an argument for buying from a brand with a written warranty, not an argument against overnight charging itself.
 Two habits improve battery health over the years: stopping your phone at around 80 percent if your device supports a charge limit, and never charging a phone under a pillow or on soft bedding where heat cannot escape. A hard bedside surface, which is what a nightstand is, is the correct environment.
 How to Add Charging to a Nightstand You Already Own
 If you like your table and just want the cables gone, you do not need a new dock. Five steps cover it, and none of them require anything beyond a tape measure.
 Measure the top and the clearance. Note the width, the depth behind where a lamp sits, and how far back the wall is. A flush pad needs about a four-inch square of clear surface.
 Pick a low-profile pad over a standing dock. If you do not prop your phone up to read, a flat Qi2 pad is shorter, cooler, and easier to place.
 Route the cable through the back. Most nightstands have a rear cutout or a shallow drawer. Feed the cord through there and keep the plug at floor level behind the table where it cannot be kicked.
 Add a clip or adhesive channel to the leg. A single cable clipped to a table leg reads as tidy. A coil of loose cord hanging behind the table does not.
 Secure the pad so it cannot be knocked. A rubber mat underneath, or a stick-on pad, stops it sliding when you reach across in the dark.
 If you want the cables gone entirely rather than reduced, the honest answer is that a single multi-device dock is still the only way to do it. That is the whole premise of this roundup.
 When a Nightstand With Built-In Charging Makes More Sense
 Built-in charging earns its place in two situations. First, when you are replacing the nightstand anyway and can choose a table with a Qi pad in the top surface, so there is no separate object and no visible cord. Second, in a guest room or a rental where drilling or running cable is not practical.
 The trade-off is charging speed. Furniture-integrated pads are usually plain Qi at 10 to 15W, with no MagSafe alignment and no fast watch charging, so you are trading convenience and looks for the ability to top up quickly. If your devices charge overnight anyway, that is a fair swap.
 We have covered the furniture side separately in our guide to the best nightstands with charging stations , which is worth reading if you are redecorating rather than just replacing a charger.
 Frequently Asked Questions
 Are nightstands with charging stations safe?
 Yes, when the charger has foreign object detection and over-temperature protection and carries FCC or UL certification. The documented overheating problems come from cheap unbranded multi-device stations. Charging a phone on a hard bedside surface overnight is safe; avoid charging under a pillow or on soft bedding, and stop your phone near 80 percent if your device supports a charge limit.
 Which is better, Qi or MagSafe?
 MagSafe and Qi2 are better for most people in 2026 because the magnets line the coils up automatically, giving faster and more reliable charging and less failed overnight charges. Plain Qi is the compatibility fallback for older iPhones and some Android handsets. Choose magnetic charging if you have an iPhone 12 or newer, or a MagSafe case.
 What is the best 3-in-1 wireless charging station?
 The Anker MagGo 3-in-1 Qi2 15W dock is the best all-round choice for a nightstand: small footprint, certified fast Apple Watch charging, cool overnight operation, and a 40W adapter in the box. For a soft ambient glow, the Ouotoo 3-in-1 adds a dimmable night light. For the fastest top-ups, the Anker Prime Qi2.2 reaches 25W.
 Does a wireless charging station come with a power adapter?
 Usually, but not always. Of the eight stations we covered, seven include a wall adapter, and the Acer Gadget 7-in-1 comes with a cable only. This is the most repeated complaint in the category, so check the in-the-box list before you buy and decide whether you already own a suitable USB-C wall charger.
 Will a wireless charger work with a phone case on?
 It depends entirely on the case thickness limit each charger states. These docks specify between 2mm and 5mm; the Acer Gadget needs under 2mm, which means most protective cases must come off. Magnetic models also need a MagSafe case or an iPhone 12 or newer for a secure hold, otherwise the phone can slide off the magnet overnight.
 Is 10W or 15W better for wireless charging?
 For overnight charging, 10W is enough, because the phone has eight hours to fill. 15W, and the 25W available on the newest Qi2.2 stations, matters when you want a fast top-up before leaving the house rather than a full overnight charge. Buy based on when you charge, not on the largest number printed on the box.
 The Verdict: Which Nightstand Charger Should You Buy?
 The Anker MagGo 3-in-1 Qi2 15W is the best wireless charging station for most nightstands, because it is small, cool, quiet, quick with a watch, and ships with its adapter. Add the Ouotoo if a dimmable night light matters to you, the Acer Gadget if two people charge phones on the same bedside table, and the Anker Prime only if you want a fast top-up rather than an overnight fill. Whichever you choose, check the case thickness limit and the in-the-box list before you order.

 What iPhone 17 owners need to know before buying
 25W is a maximum capability, not a promise
 Belkin lists wireless charging up to 25W for iPhone 17, iPhone 17 Pro, and iPhone 17 Pro Max with compatible Qi2/Qi2.2 or MagSafe-style chargers.  Choose 25W or 15W. Pick 25W for daytime top-ups and the highest advertised output on iPhone 17, 17 Pro, and 17 Pro Max. Pick 15W for overnight charging or lower cost. iPhone Air’s listed ceiling is 20W.
 Count your devices. Do not buy a 3-in-1 unless you need Apple Watch and AirPods charging. A 2-in-1 is smaller, cheaper, and simpler for many owners.
 Check the case and camera clearance. Match the manufacturer’s thickness limit to your actual case, remove wallets and magnetic accessories, and ensure the camera module does not force the phone away from the charging surface.
 Add the complete setup cost. Include the required USB-C adapter, cable, compatible magnetic case, and any separately purchased MagSafe Charger.
 Important limitations and failure modes
 “MagSafe” does not automatically mean 25W. Confirm whether the accessory is Apple MagSafe, Qi2 15W, or Qi2/Qi2.2 25W.
 A 25W label is not a guaranteed charging rate. Heat, alignment, case thickness, adapter capacity, software, and simultaneous charging can reduce output.
 Cooling does not prove faster charging. Anker’s AirCool and ESR’s CryoBoost are manufacturer features; without comparative testing, they should not be presented as independently proven winners.
 Wireless charging is not ideal for every workload. Gaming, long 4K recording, navigation in a hot car, and other demanding tasks can increase heat while the phone charges.
 3-in-1 docks add complexity. They occupy more space, cost more, may require a stronger adapter, and add more charging components that can fail.
 Landscape use must be checked by SKU. Do not infer charging orientation, angle adjustment, or camera clearance from a product photograph alone. Confirm the manufacturer’s specifications or manual for the exact model.
 Vehicle use is a separate category. A desk charging stand is not automatically safe or stable in a car. Look for a mount designed for the vehicle attachment method and vibration conditions.
 Manufacturer product pages establish specifications and compatibility, but they do not establish real charging times, hinge durability, one-handed Pro Max removal, fan noise, or long-term stability. Those qualities require independent hands-on testing and should not be assumed from a listing.
 Sources and current product information

 Belkin UltraCharge 3-in-1 compatibility and included accessories 
 Anker Prime Qi2 25W foldable 3-in-1 
 ESR CryoBoost foldable charging station 
 Apple wireless-charger catalog 
 Apple charging-essentials catalog 
 Verdict
 Choose the Belkin UltraCharge 2-in-1 Foldable for the best general-purpose balance. Choose the Belkin UltraCharge 3-in-1 if you need Apple Watch and AirPods charging. Choose Anker Prime or ESR CryoBoost when active cooling and foldable 25W charging are priorities. For a simple overnight setup, a Qi2 15W stand is enough; for a modular, non-powered display, use Twelve South Forté with Apple’s MagSafe Charger .

Bedside use is a different beast. You need a weighted base so the stand doesn’t tip when you grab your iPhone at 2 a.m. You need a sleep-friendly LED that won’t light up the bedroom. And if you care about iOS 17+ StandBy mode, the stand needs to hold the iPhone in landscape without the magnet sliding off.
 I tested each pick below for one-handed pickup, LED brightness, charging heat, and whether the phone stayed attached all night. The list mixes 3-in-1 docks for iPhone + Apple Watch + AirPods, slim 2-in-1 stands for iPhone + AirPods only, and budget pads for anyone who just wants a clean magnetic snap on a flat surface. Every pick supports iPhone 12 through iPhone 17 series and most work through a standard MagSafe case.

I left it on my nightstand for three weeks straight, and it never tipped when I grabbed my phone one-handed in the dark.
 The included 18W adapter is a quiet win. A lot of nightstand chargers skip the wall adapter to hit a low price, then you end up paying for a GaN brick anyway. Anlmz includes a 3.3ft USB-C cable plus a 2-year warranty, which is rare for a charger at this price tier.
 One quirk worth flagging: this is a center-place wireless charger, not true MagSafe with magnets. The phone snaps into a sweet spot but you do have to nudge it into position. After a couple of nights it became second nature. Through a thin MagSafe case (under 2.5mm) it works fine; thicker cases need to come off.
 The blue LED is soft enough to not blast the bedroom, but I would have loved a hard off switch. Still, at 42k+ reviews and a 4.2-star average, this is the most-tested budget 3-in-1 on Amazon, and our testing matched the crowd: it just works as a nightstand charger.

 The Eazpower 3-level nightlight is the most configurable in this roundup. High, medium, low, and off – all touch-controlled. On my nightstand I set it to low as a soft amber glow. It’s the only charger I tested where the night light genuinely helped me navigate a dark bedroom without grabbing my phone.
 The 20W Quick Charge adapter is included, so this works out of the box. The 2-year warranty is also a strong sign of build confidence at this price tier.

 Who should buy this

 Who should skip this

 What to Look for in a MagSafe Nightstand Charger
 Buying a MagSafe charger for a nightstand is different from buying one for a desk. The constraints are tighter: limited space, total darkness when you reach for the phone, and 8 hours of unattended charging. Here’s what our testing surfaced.
 MagSafe vs Qi2 vs Qi2 25W: What You Actually Need
 Apple’s MagSafe is a magnetic ring that aligns the iPhone’s charging coil and delivers up to 15W (iPhone 12-15) or 25W (iPhone 16 and 17 with Qi2 25W / Qi2.2 certification). Qi2 is the open standard that mimics MagSafe’s magnetic alignment – any Qi2-certified pad will give the same 15W speeds as Apple’s own puck. Qi2 25W (sometimes called Qi2.2) is the newer spec that unlocks 25W for iPhone 16 and 17.
 For a nightstand, you don’t need 25W. Overnight charging at 15W is gentler on the battery, generates less heat, and keeps the charger cooler to the touch. Save the 25W pads for desk use where you want a quick top-up.
 StandBy Mode 101: Charging in Landscape
 StandBy mode activates when you charge an iPhone 12 or newer in landscape while it’s propped up. The screen shows a clock, photos, weather, or widgets. To enable it, plug in your iPhone sideways on a MagSafe stand, then go to Settings > StandBy and turn it on.
 For nightstand use, look for a stand with at least a 60° vertical tilt and stable landscape support. Our top picks (#1, #2, #7, #10) all nail this. Pads and flat chargers don’t support StandBy mode at all.
 Overnight Charging Safety: Heat, Battery, and Sleep
 Yes, it’s safe to leave your iPhone on a MagSafe charger overnight. iOS includes Optimized Battery Charging that learns your routine and holds the charge at 80% until you need it. Modern MagSafe chargers also have temperature cutoffs that throttle or stop charging if the phone gets too warm.
 For a quiet bedroom, prioritize chargers with sleep-friendly LEDs (auto-off, dim, or fully toggleable). Avoid actively-cooled 25W chargers that use small fans – they can produce a low hum that’s audible at night.
 Nightstand-Specific Features That Matter
 Five things separate a great nightstand charger from a generic desk charger: weighted base (so it doesn’t tip on one-handed pickup), short footprint (under 4 inches deep), no bright LED or auto-off LED, landscape StandBy support, and a USB-C PD adapter included in the box.
 Reddit users in r/MagSafe consistently call out one-handed pickup as the #1 nightstand requirement. If you have to use two hands to grab your phone, the charger is wrong for a nightstand.
 Cable Management and Sleep-Friendly Design
 A 5ft cable is the minimum for a nightstand – shorter cables force the charger too close to the wall outlet. Look for chargers that include a 1.5m or longer USB-C cable. If the cable runs behind furniture, use simple adhesive cable clips to keep the nightstand tidy.
 For dark-sleep bedrooms, prioritize matte black or dark gray finishes over glossy white. A glossy charger reflects any ambient light (LEDs, streetlight through curtains) and amplifies the visual clutter.
 Frequently Asked Questions
 Which MagSafe charger is best for a nightstand?
 The best MagSafe charger for a nightstand depends on how many Apple devices you charge. For iPhone + Apple Watch + AirPods, the Anlmz 3-in-1 Charging Station is our top pick because of its weighted base, included 18W adapter, and soft blue LED. For iPhone + AirPods only, the UGREEN MagFlow 2-in-1 is the most premium-feeling option. For travel, the RYND Foldable 3-in-1 doubles as a home nightstand charger.
 Is it OK to leave an iPhone on a MagSafe charger overnight?
 Yes, it’s safe to leave your iPhone on a MagSafe charger overnight. iOS includes Optimized Battery Charging, which holds the battery at 80% until it learns you need a full charge. Modern MagSafe chargers also have temperature cutoffs that throttle charging if the phone gets too warm. For best battery longevity, pair overnight MagSafe charging with a 15W or Qi2-certified charger rather than a 25W actively-cooled pad.
 What are the downsides of using MagSafe chargers?
 The main downsides of MagSafe chargers are slower charging than wired (15W vs 20W+ for USB-C PD), more heat generation under load, and the need to remove thick cases (over 3mm) for reliable magnetic alignment. MagSafe is also less efficient than wired charging, which means more wasted energy as heat. For overnight use these downsides are minor, but for quick top-ups a wired charger is still faster.
 Why is MagSafe discontinued?
 MagSafe is not discontinued – it is Apple’s magnetic charging ecosystem that launched with iPhone 12 in 2020. The original Apple MagSafe Charger puck (1m) was discontinued in 2026 and replaced by the Apple MagSafe Charger (2 m) which supports 25W charging on iPhone 16 and 17. The MagSafe name now covers Apple’s entire magnetic accessory line, including cases, wallets, and battery packs.
 What wattage MagSafe charger do I need for fast charging?
 For iPhone 12 through 15, you need a 15W MagSafe or Qi2-certified charger for full-speed wireless charging. For iPhone 16 and iPhone 17, you need a Qi2 25W (Qi2.2) certified charger to unlock the full 25W wireless speed. For overnight nightstand use, a 15W charger is plenty and gentler on the battery than 25W. Make sure to pair the charger with a USB-C PD adapter rated 20W or higher.
 Final Verdict: Which MagSafe Charger Should Sit on Your Nightstand?
 After testing 18 different chargers over three months, our best overall MagSafe charger for a nightstand remains the Anlmz 3-in-1 Charging Station – it charges iPhone, Apple Watch, and AirPods simultaneously, includes the 18W adapter in the box, and has a soft LED that won’t blast the bedroom. For a single-device stand with the best viewing angle, the MagSafe 3-in-1 Stand (B0CNTH3F7P) is our best value pick, especially for StandBy mode users.
 If you’re building a complete bedside setup, also check out our guide to the best leather valet trays for nightstands – they pair perfectly with a MagSafe charger to keep keys, watches, and small items tidy. For travelers who want one charger for home and the road, the RYND Foldable 3-in-1 doubles as both a nightstand stand and a suitcase companion.
 Whatever you choose, prioritize a weighted base, a sleep-friendly LED, and an included USB-C PD adapter. Those three details separate a charger that’s just okay on a nightstand from one that’s perfect. Updated September 2026 with new Qi2 25W picks for iPhone 16 and 17 owners.

Nightstand Wireless Charger: Anker vs. Belkin vs. Mophie 
 Skip to content 
 Nightstand Charging for Three Devices Without Three Bricks
 By
 PicksWeTrust Editorial Team
 ·
 August 13, 2026 
 Some links on our site may earn us a commission at no extra cost to you. Learn more . 
 Published August 13, 2026. Prices and specs checked September 13, 2026. 
 Three devices, one nightstand outlet, and cables that never stay untangled by morning — that’s the actual problem a nightstand wireless charger solves. There’s no single “best overall” pick here anymore. The Anker MagGo 3-in-1 Charging Station has the smallest footprint and is the only one with Apple’s own Watch certification. Belkin’s BoostCharge Pro is the cheapest and simplest. The Mophie 3-in-1 Wireless Charging Stand now undercuts Anker on price while including the most in the box. Which one is actually right for you depends on what’s charging on your nightstand every night, so that’s how we’ve organized this.
 A cluttered nightstand isn’t just an aesthetic problem for me. During hurricane season here, the last thing I want to be fumbling for after the power blinks back on is which cable goes to which brick. I’ve run a few different multi-device chargers over the years, and the ones that earn a permanent spot by the bed are the ones I don’t have to think about at 2 a.m.
 Which Nightstand Wireless Charger Fits You
 Best for an iPhone-only nightstand: Anker MagGo 3-in-1 — Apple’s own “Made for Watch” certification, plus the smallest footprint.
 Best for a mixed Android/Apple household: Belkin BoostCharge Pro — cheapest of the three, and a flat pad works the same for Android either way.
 Best for nightly watch and earbuds charging: Mophie 3-in-1 — only one with a stated two-year warranty and a fully bundled cable and adapter.
 Best for a small, crowded nightstand: Anker MagGo 3-in-1 — roughly 3.5 inches square, the smallest of the three.
 Full Nightstand Wireless Charger Spec Comparison
 Here’s the full spec rundown, pulled directly from each brand’s current listing for the models sold today.

 Belkin BoostCharge Pro 3-in-1 Wireless Charging Stand 15W / 5W / 5W Qi2-certified; MagSafe-compatible 36W power supply Not listed on Belkin’s product page Not published; described as a compact fixed stand $89.99 
 Mophie 3-in-1 Wireless Charging Stand 15W / 5W / 5W MagSafe-compatible and Certified Qi2 40W wall charger 1.5m USB-C cable 6.7 × 4.5 × 5.4 in $99.95 
 Prices are approximate, current as of publication, and change frequently — confirm the latest price with the retailer before buying. 
 A note on the Anker price: Anker’s own product page currently lists the MagGo 3-in-1 at $109.99 — up from the $89.99 we recorded previously. That single change reorders which stand wins on value, since Mophie now costs $10 less than Anker. Mophie also includes more in the box, so we’ve rebuilt the scenarios and math below around the current prices rather than leaving the old figure standing.
 Nightstand Wireless Charger for an iPhone-Only Setup
 If every device charging tonight is an Apple product, the Anker MagGo 3-in-1 Charging Station is the pick. Its Apple Watch puck carries Apple’s own “Made for Watch” magnetic charging certification, not just Qi2. Belkin and Mophie both describe themselves as “MagSafe-compatible” rather than carrying that specific Apple accessory badge, a distinction independent outlets have flagged as worth knowing about. Apple only recently opened its 15W accessory certification program to third parties at all, according to reporting from ChargerLAB . In practice, “MagSafe-compatible” stands can misalign slightly more often than one carrying Apple’s own accessory certification — a real, if minor, dealbreaker if perfect magnetic snap matters to you. For a deeper breakdown of exactly how MagSafe and Qi2 alignment differ, see our MagSafe vs. Qi2 vs. multi-device charger comparison .
 Nightstand Wireless Charger for a Mixed Household
 If your nightstand also needs to charge a Pixel, a Galaxy, or any other non-Apple phone, the Belkin BoostCharge Pro is the more sensible buy. None of these three magnetic pucks snap a non-Apple phone into place the way they do an iPhone, since the magnet ring is part of Apple’s MagSafe ecosystem. An Android phone just sits flat on the pad no matter which stand you buy, so paying for a certification your phone can’t use doesn’t make sense. Belkin’s simple, fixed 90° design with a non-slip base is the least fussy option for a phone that isn’t relying on magnetic alignment anyway, and at $89.99 it’s also the cheapest of the three. Worth noting: a handful of newer Android flagships, including some Galaxy S25 models, do ship Qi2-ready or work with cases that restore magnetic snap. That narrows this gap somewhat if your household is upgrading soon.
 For Someone Who Also Charges a Watch and Earbuds Every Night
 If you’re topping off a phone, a watch, and earbuds every single night without exception, the Mophie 3-in-1 Wireless Charging Stand is worth a look first. At its current $99.95 price, it’s no longer even the most expensive option on this list. It’s the only one of the three that explicitly bundles both a 40W wall charger and a 1.5m USB-C cable. It’s also the only one carrying a stated two-year warranty, a real consideration for a device that’s plugged in and running every night of the year. Its head also tilts flat enough to support landscape StandBy mode, a feature neither Anker’s nor Belkin’s listing mentions.
 Nightstand Wireless Charger for a Small, Crowded Space
 After years of squeezing gadgets onto a cramped nightstand, the Anker MagGo 3-in-1 Charging Station is the one I’d point a friend toward, since its 3.5-inch footprint barely dents the space. Compare that to Mophie’s 6.7-by-4.5-inch footprint, the tradeoff Mophie makes for its landscape-capable tilting head. Belkin doesn’t publish exact stand dimensions at all, which makes it the hardest of the three to plan real desk space around before it arrives. If a crowded nightstand is your main constraint, our sunrise alarm clock comparison covers the other gadget most likely to be competing for that same outlet.
 Every stand in this comparison charges the watch at the same 5W ceiling — 
 How Qi2 Certification Works for a Nightstand Wireless Charger
 All three chargers cap out at identical numbers on paper: 15W for the phone, 5W for the watch, 5W for the earbuds. That’s because all three are built around the same Qi2 Magnetic Power Profile, the wireless charging standard maintained by the Wireless Power Consortium . That standard is the reason a Qi2-certified stand snaps a phone into alignment the way Apple’s own MagSafe charger does, since the magnet ring Qi2 uses was contributed to the standard by Apple in the first place. Running a phone, watch, and earbuds at their full rated wattage simultaneously draws 25W minimum (15W + 5W + 5W) from whatever adapter is plugged into the wall. That’s a figure none of the three brands publish directly, but one that’s simple to compute from their own spec sheets.

 Anker MagGo 3-in-1 40W 25W (15+5+5) 15W (60% margin) $109.99 $2.75

 Mophie 3-in-1 40W 25W (15+5+5) 15W (60% margin) $99.95 $2.50 
 Anker and Mophie both ship the same 40W adapter headroom, but Mophie now does it for $10 less at list price, a reversal from when Anker was the cheaper of the two. Belkin’s bundled 36W adapter has the thinnest margin above what all three pucks can draw at once. That’s the kind of spec gap that doesn’t show up until you actually load all three charging spots simultaneously.
 Nightstand Wireless Charger Feature Density Per Dollar
 Spec sheets list a price and a feature list, but they don’t do the division for you. We counted eight comparable features across all three stands’ current listings, then divided each one’s current price by its count. The result is a genuinely different ranking than the sticker price alone suggests.

 Run the math and Mophie is the clear feature-density winner, at $14.28 per feature, less than half of Anker’s $27.50 and Belkin’s $30.00. That doesn’t automatically make it the “best” stand for every nightstand. Anker still wins outright on footprint and Apple Watch certification, and Belkin still wins on flat sticker price. But if you’re weighing what you’re actually getting for the money, Mophie’s bundle is the one that adds up best right now.

 We built this comparison from each manufacturer’s current published spec sheets and pricing, re-verified this session, and cross-checked it against independent reporting for certification nuances rather than claiming hands-on testing of our own. Where wattage, certification, or box contents weren’t published, we said so directly instead of guessing. Our full methodology is explained on our editorial standards page.
 Prices are approximate, current as of publication, and change frequently — confirm the latest price with the retailer before buying. 
 Nightstand Wireless Charger Questions
 Do All Three of These Chargers Hit 15W on an iPhone?
 Yes, on a Qi2-certified iPhone (iPhone 12 or newer), all three deliver up to 15W to the phone puck, per each manufacturer’s own spec sheet. Older non-Qi2 phones drop to the base Qi ceiling of 7.5W or lower, since the extra wattage requires the magnetic alignment that Qi2 defines, according to the Wireless Power Consortium’s Qi2 standard.
 Can I charge an Android phone on one of these stations?
 Most Android flagships released in the last two years support Qi or Qi2 charging, so they’ll charge on the flat pad, but without the magnets they won’t snap into place the way an iPhone does. A handful of newer Android phones, including some Galaxy S25 models, ship Qi2-ready or work with cases that restore the magnetic snap.
 Why did the Anker MagGo’s price change?
 Anker’s own product listing currently shows the MagGo 3-in-1 at $109.99, up from the $89.99 we had recorded in an earlier version of this comparison. Wireless charger pricing shifts often with sales and promotions on all three brands’ sites, which is exactly why we recommend confirming the current price before buying rather than trusting any single snapshot, including this one.
 Is “Qi2 certified” the same thing as Apple’s MagSafe?
 Not quite. Qi2’s magnetic alignment system is based on the magnet array Apple contributed to the standard, so a Qi2-certified charger snaps into place similarly to MagSafe, but it’s tested by the Wireless Power Consortium rather than carrying Apple’s own separate accessory certification. Of the three stands in this comparison, only the Anker MagGo currently advertises an Apple accessory certification badge — for the Apple Watch puck specifically — on its listing.
 Do I need to buy a separate power adapter for any of these?
 No. All three ship with their own USB-C power adapter in the box, rated between 36W and 40W depending on the brand, so there’s nothing extra to buy just to get the station running out of the box.
 Will leaving my phone on one of these overnight damage the battery?
 No — all three use standard temperature-controlled charging chips that taper output once your phone reports a full charge, the same safeguard built into Apple’s own MagSafe charger. Overnight charging on any of these three carries no more risk than plugging into a wall charger, though earbuds are still worth pulling off the pad occasionally if you’re also using them for calls during the day; our guide to budget wireless earbuds covers battery longevity in more depth.

 How to Choose a Wireless Charger for Your Nightstand
 LED behavior comes first for bedrooms. The single most common complaint in our forum research was bright indicator lights disturbing sleep. Look for chargers that dim automatically like the INIU, turn off mid-charge like the TOZO, or offer a full brightness kill switch like the ANJANK clock.
 Match the standard to your phone. iPhones benefit most from Qi2 or MagSafe magnetic chargers, which snap into alignment and enable StandBy mode. Android phones charge fastest on Qi pads that support 15W Extended Power Profile, like the INIU or TOZO with the right adapter.
 Count your devices honestly. If you charge a phone, Watch, and AirPods every night, a 3-in-1 station such as the Anker MagGo or Belkin beats three separate pads on clutter and outlet usage. Single-phone users can save money with a basic stand.
 Check your case thickness. Magnetic chargers demand thin, MagSafe-friendly cases, while the TOZO tolerates cases up to 5-6mm. If you use a rugged case and refuse to remove it nightly, a high-tolerance pad is the safer bet.
 Consider stability and one-handed use. A weighted base matters when you grab the phone half-asleep. Forum users consistently praised bottom-heavy stands and magnetic snap-on designs for exactly this reason.
 Decide whether StandBy mode matters to you. iPhone users who want a bedside clock display need a stand or adjustable charger that holds the phone in landscape, like the MagGo or the Anker 313. Flat pads cannot do this.
 Frequently Asked Questions
 What is the best wireless charger for a nightstand?
 The Anker MagGo Qi2 3-in-1 Charging Station is the best overall pick for most nightstands. It charges an iPhone, Apple Watch, and AirPods simultaneously, supports StandBy mode in landscape, and includes its power adapter. For single-phone budgets, the Yootech 10W stand is the best value option.
 Are wireless chargers safe to leave on a nightstand overnight?
 Yes. Certified Qi, Qi2, and MagSafe chargers include over-temperature, over-current, and short-circuit protection, and modern phones stop drawing power once full. Placing the charger on a hard surface rather than fabric, and using the included or specified adapter, keeps temperatures lowest.
 Do wireless chargers work with thick phone cases?
 Most work through cases up to about 3mm, and models like the TOZO W1 Max handle cases up to 5-6mm. Magnetic MagSafe and Qi2 chargers are the exception, since thick cases weaken the magnet connection and can slow or stop charging.
 Is MagSafe or Qi better for a nightstand?
 MagSafe (and Qi2) is better for iPhones because magnets guarantee perfect alignment and enable StandBy clock mode with one-handed placement. Plain Qi is better for Android phones, since devices like Samsung Galaxies charge at up to 15W on certified Qi pads without magnets.
 What is the best wireless charger for a nightstand with no light?
 The TOZO W1 Max and the Yootech stand are the best no-light options. Both use sleep-friendly LEDs that turn off or dim completely during charging, so your bedroom stays dark all night.
 Conclusion
 The Anker MagGo Qi2 3-in-1 remains our top recommendation among the best wireless chargers for nightstands in 2026, because it clears the most clutter and charges every core Apple device fast. The Yootech stand covers single-phone users on a budget, and the Anker Prime 25W handles speed demons and frequent travelers.
 Whichever you choose, prioritize the sleep-friendly details: dimming LEDs, a stable base, and compatibility with your actual case. Your future self, reaching for a fully charged phone at 6 a.m. in a dark and quiet room, will thank you.

 How We Tested the Best Wireless Chargers for Nightstands
 Every charger in this guide spent at least three weeks on my nightstand charging my iPhone 15 Pro Max, an Apple Watch Series 10, AirPods Pro and occasionally a Samsung Galaxy S24 or Pixel 8. I paid attention to the things that actually matter on a nightstand rather than the things that look good on a spec sheet.
 I tracked charging speed from 0% to 100% overnight, measured how warm the phone got, watched for fan noise, checked whether the LED indicators stayed awake all night, and tested alignment with three different case styles. I also looked at how stable each dock was when I grabbed the phone one-handed in the dark – the most underrated test for any bedside charger.
 I cross-referenced my experience with thousands of verified buyer reviews from Amazon to confirm that my impressions matched what other buyers experienced over months of use, not just days. The result is a list weighted heavily toward chargers with proven long-term reliability, not just impressive spec sheets. The same patience-based testing approach is what we use across all our wireless gear guides here, including our roundup of the best wireless microphones for YouTube .
 What to Look for in a Wireless Charger for Your Nightstand
 Not all wireless chargers are good nightstand chargers. A great bedside wireless charger needs to satisfy a different set of requirements than a great desk charger. Here’s what I paid attention to while testing the picks in this guide.
 Qi2 vs MagSafe vs Qi – Which Standard Do You Actually Need
 The three wireless charging standards you’ll see most often are Qi, Qi2 and MagSafe. Qi is the original inductive standard, supports up to 15W on supported Android phones and 7.5W on iPhones, and works with almost anything. Qi2 is the newer magnetic standard – it adds MagSafe-style alignment magnets to Qi and supports 15W charging on iPhones that are Qi2 certified. MagSafe is Apple’s own magnetic standard, which is compatible with Qi2 devices.
 For a nightstand, the standard matters less than you’d think. You’re charging for 6-8 hours, so the difference between 7.5W and 15W is academic. What matters more is whether your phone aligns reliably every night. Qi2 and MagSafe chargers use magnets to snap the phone into the perfect spot, which means you can drop the phone down half-asleep and wake up to a full battery. Plain Qi pads require more careful placement.
 If you have an iPhone 12 or newer, a Qi2 or MagSafe charger is the easiest nightstand experience. If you have an older iPhone or an Android phone, a plain Qi stand like the Anker 313 or NANAMI is plenty.
 Stand vs Pad – Which Form Factor Fits Your Bedside
 Stand-style chargers hold your phone upright, which makes them perfect for iPhone StandBy mode, glancing at notifications, Face ID unlock without picking up the phone, and watching video while charging. Pad-style chargers lie flat, which makes them more discreet but means you can’t see the screen without picking the phone up.
 For nightstand use, I’d recommend a stand for most people. The ability to see the time, notifications and weather at a glance – and to unlock the phone with Face ID without picking it up – is more valuable at a bedside than it is at a desk. Pads make more sense if you want a truly minimal nightstand look, or if you’re charging multiple devices and need the flat surface area.
 LED Glare, Fan Noise and Sleep Hygiene
 The single most common complaint about bedside wireless chargers in user reviews is LED glare. A small blue or green LED that you can ignore in an office becomes a glaring beacon at 2 a.m. Look for chargers that either have no LEDs at all (the ZealSound), LEDs that dim automatically (the JARGOU), or LEDs that you can manually turn off (the GETPALS and Y888).
 Cooling fans are the second most common complaint. Some high-wattage Qi2 25W chargers include a small fan to keep the phone cool under heavy load. On a nightstand, even a quiet fan is audible when everything else is silent. The chargers in this guide are all fan-free, which is one reason they’re on the list.
 For sleep hygiene, the bigger question is whether to charge your phone next to your bed at all. Research on bedroom EMF from phones is mixed, and most modern phones stop transmitting once the battery is full. If you’re concerned, an invisible under-mount charger like the Kew Labs UTS-2 lets you charge through a nightstand surface so the phone sits several inches from your head.
 Case Thickness, Wattage and Charging Speed
 Most modern wireless chargers work through cases up to 4-5mm thick, which covers virtually every standard case. The exceptions are cases with metal plates, magnetic ring attachments (PopSocket metal rings, for example), or very thick rugged cases. If you use a MagSafe-compatible case, you also get the benefit of magnetic alignment on Qi2 and MagSafe chargers.
 Charging speed on a nightstand is mostly irrelevant. Even at 7.5W, an iPhone charges from dead to full in about 3-4 hours, and you’re typically sleeping for 6-8 hours. The only time wattage matters is if you want to charge something other than a phone – a tablet or a power bank – or if you only have a few hours before you need the device again. The same principle is why our wireless microphones for weddings guide prioritizes reliable long-form recording over peak specs that don’t matter in real ceremonies.
 Aesthetic Finishes and Nightstand Decor
 A wireless charger that lives on your nightstand is part of your bedroom decor. The black plastic puck look works in an office, but a leather-wrapped pad or an aluminum stand often fits better next to a lamp, a stack of books and a glass of water.
 The PU leather finish on the ZealSound pad is the most furniture-like option in this guide. The aluminum UGREEN MagFlow is the most premium-feeling. The Y888 3-in-1 stand with its ambient night light is the most “designed for the bedroom” option. If your nightstand style matters, pick the charger that matches your decor rather than just the fastest spec sheet.
 Frequently Asked Questions
 What is the best wireless charger for a nightstand?
 The best wireless charger for a nightstand is one that charges reliably overnight, has a dimmable or no LED indicator, runs silently, and fits your device ecosystem. Our top pick is the Anker 313 Wireless Charger Stand for its reliability, 127k+ verified reviews, and proven case compatibility. For Apple households wanting one dock for iPhone, Apple Watch and AirPods, the Anker MagGo 3-in-1 Qi2 is the best premium upgrade.
 Is MagSafe or Qi better?
 MagSafe is Apple’s magnetic standard that supports 15W charging on iPhones 12 and newer with perfect magnetic alignment. Qi is the universal inductive standard that works with iPhones and Android phones but caps at 7.5W on iPhones unless the charger is Qi2 certified. Qi2 is the newer standard that adds MagSafe-style magnets to Qi and supports 15W charging on iPhones. For nightstand use, the standard matters less than alignment – magnetic chargers let you drop the phone down without precise placement.
 Can wireless chargers work through a case?
 Yes, most wireless chargers work through non-metallic cases up to 4-5mm thick, including plastic, silicone, leather and TPU. Metal plates, magnetic ring attachments like PopSocket metal rings, and very thick rugged cases can block charging. If you use a MagSafe-compatible case, you also get magnetic alignment on Qi2 and MagSafe chargers for easier placement.
 What are some good charging stations for nightstands?
 Good charging stations for nightstands include 3-in-1 docks like the Anker MagGo for Apple households, the Y888 3-in-1 stand for the strongest magnets and ambient lighting, the GETPALS foldable for travel, and the Anlmz 3-in-1 for the best budget multi-device dock. For shared nightstands or families, the Acer Gadget 7-in-1 handles up to seven devices from one outlet. For light sleepers, the JARGOU’s auto-shut-off LEDs and the ZealSound’s light-free PU leather pad are the best options.
 Is there a downside to wireless charging?
 The main downsides of wireless charging are slower speeds than wired fast charging, heat generation under heavy load, and the inability to use the phone while it’s charging without lifting it off the pad. Wireless charging is also slightly less efficient than wired, which means more heat and a small amount of wasted energy. For nightstand use these downsides are minor because you have 6-8 hours to charge, the phone just sits there, and modern chargers manage heat well.
 How many watts do I need for a nightstand wireless charger?
 For a nightstand wireless charger, 7.5W to 15W is plenty because you have 6-8 hours to charge overnight. Higher wattage like Qi2 25W matters more at a desk where you want a fast top-up before a meeting. The exception is if you want to charge multiple devices at once – a 3-in-1 dock needs at least 15W total to charge an iPhone, Apple Watch and AirPods simultaneously at reasonable speed.
 The Best Wireless Charger for Your Nightstand
 After three months of testing, the Anker 313 Wireless Charger Stand remains the wireless charger I trust most on my nightstand. Its 127,000+ verified reviews, reliable case compatibility, and proven long-term durability make it the safest recommendation for anyone who just wants their phone to wake up fully charged without thinking about it. For most people looking for the best wireless chargers for nightstands, that’s exactly what matters.
 If you’re an Apple household and want one tidy dock for iPhone, Apple Watch and AirPods, step up to the Anker MagGo 3-in-1 Qi2 – the Qi2 magnets and Apple Watch fast-charging make it the most premium bedside experience in 2026. If you’re on a tighter budget, the NANAMI 2-coil stand delivers reliable charging at a price that makes it easy to put one on every nightstand in the house.
 For light sleepers, the JARGOU’s auto-shut-off LEDs or the ZealSound’s light-free PU leather pad solve the most common bedside complaint about wireless chargers. For frequent travelers, the GETPALS foldable replaces three cables in your bag. For families sharing a nightstand, the Acer Gadget 7-in-1 handles everything from one outlet. Pick the one that matches your ecosystem and sleep style, and you’ll never fumble for a cable in the dark again.

 A wireless charger passes power to the phone through a coil under its surface, so the phone has to sit over that spot to charge. Chargers come as flat pads or as stands that hold the phone upright with the screen in view, and magnetic versions cling to an iPhone 12 or later, or another Qi2 phone, and line themselves up.
 None of these comes with a wall plug, and the USB adapter you pair one with decides how fast the phone charges. The stands without magnets work with any phone that charges wirelessly, Androids and older iPhones included. The magnetic chargers here also charge an AirPods case that supports wireless charging.
 What matters
 Qi or Qi2 certification, rather than a vague fast-charging claim.
 A cable long enough to reach from the outlet to the bed.
 How thick a case it charges through, or a MagSafe case.
 A light that dims at night, for the nightstand.

 Apple’s own magnetic charger snaps onto the back of an iPhone 12 or later and charges at up to 25W on an iPhone 16, 17 or Air with a 30W adapter, and up to 15W on older MagSafe iPhones. The 6.6 ft cable reaches from the outlet to the bed or the couch, so the phone can stay in hand while it charges.
 What owners say: Fast charging and a grip that survives a knock or two win the most praise. It can run hot for some, durability divides owners, and a handful find the finish nicks and scratches easily.
 Heads up: There’s no plug in the box: Apple’s 30W USB-C adapter, sold separately, unlocks the 25W speed.
 A closer look: An iPhone 8 to 11 still charges on it, at up to 7.5W but without the magnetic hold, so center the phone. A MagSafe case, or none, gives the firmest grip, while thick or metal-backed cases get in the way. The cable is built in, so a frayed one means a new charger.
